evidence.claim: Varadhan, Asymptotic probabilities and differential equations, CPAM 19 (1966): paper that began a general theory of large deviations
Abel citation (quoted on MacTutor) credits the 1966 paper as the start of a general large-deviation theory
Cramer 1938 limit theorem for rare deviations of sums (precursor, insurance context)

conceptual.note: Taken as the first public general formulation (variational principle and Laplace-type asymptotics). Earlier precursors with published records: Cramer 1938 (Actualites sci. industr. 736), Sanov 1957/1961, Schilder 1966 (Trans. AMS, doi 10.1090/s0002-9947-1966-0201892-6). Wikipedia large-deviations page notes Einstein 1907 fluctuation ideas; not used as date.

evidence.claim: Donsker and Varadhan, Asymptotic evaluation of certain Markov process expectations for large time, I, CPAM 28 (1975)
MacTutor: joint Donsker-Varadhan papers on hierarchy of large deviations for Markov processes, entropy-type minimisation
Lanford, Entropy and equilibrium states in classical statistical mechanics, LNP 20 (1973): statistical-mechanics route to large deviations
evidence.source: Crossref record; volume year 1973 from zbMATH 0253.00011

methodological.note: Donsker-Varadhan I-IV (1975, 1975, 1976, 1983) apply a free-energy-like variational formula to occupation measures of Markov processes. Lanford 1973 (Battelle 1971 rencontres) is an explicit statistical-mechanics treatment; which counts as the import event is a judgement call. Wiener-sausage and polaron applications came later.

evidence.claim: Earliest zbMATH title containing "large deviations": Weingarten 1956, Ann. Math. Stat. 27
evidence.source: zbMATH Open search ti:"large deviations" py:1900-1959 (7 hits)

evidence.claim: Groeneboom 1980, Large deviations and asymptotic efficiencies, Mathematical Centre Tracts 118: earliest book title found
Varadhan 1984, Large deviations and applications, CBMS-NSF 46 lecture series
Ellis 1985, Entropy, large deviations, and statistical mechanics, Grundlehren 271

institutional.note: Phrase in paper titles from 1956 (probability of sums); dedicated monographs 1980 (Groeneboom), 1984 (Varadhan CBMS lectures; Stroock Universitext zbMATH 0552.60022), 1985 (Ellis, explicitly linking to statistical mechanics), 1989 (Deuschel-Stroock). Result is the earliest indexed title in zbMATH, not an absolute first use.

works.citation: Varadhan, S. R. S. Asymptotic probabilities and differential equations. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 19 (1966) 261-286.
works.whyItMatters: General large-deviation framework and Varadhan lemma.

works.citation: Varadhan, S. R. S. Large deviations and applications. CBMS-NSF Regional Conf. Ser. Appl. Math. 46, SIAM (1984).
Donsker, M. D.; Varadhan, S. R. S. Asymptotic evaluation of certain Markov process expectations for large time, I. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 28 (1975).
works.whyItMatters: Occupation-measure large deviations via a variational (free-energy type) formula.

works.citation: Donsker, M. D.; Varadhan, S. R. S. Asymptotic evaluation of certain Markov process expectations for large time, III. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 29 (1976).
works.whyItMatters: Extends the programme to general Markov processes.

works.citation: Cramer, H. Sur un nouveau theoreme-limite de la theorie des probabilites. Actualites Sci. Ind. 736 (1938) 5-23.
works.whyItMatters: First rigorous large-deviation estimate for sums; precursor.

notes: Event framed as import from physics: the free-energy / entropy analogy is explicit in Ellis 1985 and Lanford 1973; Varadhan and Donsker framed it probabilistically. Freidlin-Wentzell small-noise theory (1970s; English book 1984, Grundlehren 260) is a parallel strand not cited as a person here because only chapter-level DOIs were checked. Priority between Cramer (1938) and Varadhan (1966) as "origin" depends on whether the conceptual date means the estimate or the general principle.

aliases: P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits

evidence.claim: Yao, Theory and application of trapdoor functions, FOCS 1982: pseudorandomness from computational hardness
Blum and Micali, How to generate cryptographically strong sequences of pseudo random bits, FOCS 1982 (SIAM J. Comput. 1984)

conceptual.note: The general idea that hardness yields pseudorandomness (and so derandomisation) is public in the 1982 cryptographic papers. The specific non-cryptographic version, a function hard for small circuits plus combinatorial designs, is Nisan-Wigderson 1988 (see methodological). If the event is read narrowly, conceptual = 1988.

evidence.claim: Nisan and Wigderson, Hardness vs. randomness, 29th FOCS (1988)
Journal version: Nisan and Wigderson, Hardness vs randomness, J. Comput. Syst. Sci. 49 (1994) 149-167
Nisan, Pseudorandom bits for constant depth circuits, Combinatorica 11 (1991): uses parity lower bounds to fool AC0

methodological.note: NW 1988 builds the design-based generator from any hard function. Later milestone: Impagliazzo-Wigderson 1997 (STOC, doi 10.1145/258533.258590) P = BPP if E needs exponential circuits.

evidence.claim: Paper title "Hardness vs. randomness" (FOCS 1988) names the area
Nisan and Wigderson, Hardness vs. randomness - a survey, Structure in Complexity Theory 1989

institutional.note: zbMATH title search: "hardness vs randomness" 8 hits, earliest 1994 JCSS; "hardness versus randomness" 4 hits, earliest 2003. Crossref gives the 1988 FOCS title. No textbook, chair or MSC code naming it found; earliest indexed title only.

works.citation: Nisan, N.; Wigderson, A. Hardness vs. randomness. Proc. 29th FOCS (1988).
works.whyItMatters: Introduces the design-based generator from hard functions.

works.citation: Nisan, N.; Wigderson, A. Hardness vs randomness. J. Comput. Syst. Sci. 49 (1994) 149-167.
Nisan, N. Pseudorandom bits for constant depth circuits. Combinatorica 11 (1991).
works.whyItMatters: Lower bound turned into generator for constant-depth circuits.

works.citation: Nisan, N.; Wigderson, A. Hardness vs. randomness. Proc. 29th FOCS (1988).
Impagliazzo, R.; Wigderson, A. P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits: derandomizing the XOR lemma. Proc. 29th STOC (1997).
works.whyItMatters: Strongest form of the hardness-randomness trade-off.

works.citation: Impagliazzo, R.; Wigderson, A. P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits. Proc. 29th STOC (1997).
works.whyItMatters: Derandomises BPP under a uniform circuit lower bound.

notes: Yao (1982) and Blum-Micali (1982) are cryptographic precursors; not listed as people because biography pages were not checked. Whether the event starts in 1982 (hardness to pseudorandomness in general) or 1988 (circuit hardness plus designs) is a scope question.

canonicalName: Measure rigidity applied to the Littlewood conjecture and arithmetic QUE

evidence.claim: Furstenberg, Disjointness in ergodic theory, minimal sets, and a problem in Diophantine approximation, Math. Systems Theory 1 (1967)
Cassels and Swinnerton-Dyer 1955 (product of three linear forms); their conjecture implies Littlewood
evidence.source: Crossref record; implication per Wikipedia Littlewood conjecture page

evidence.claim: Margulis 2000, Problems and conjectures in rigidity theory (Mathematics: frontiers and perspectives, AMS)

conceptual.note: Taken as the first published joining of rigidity for multiplicative (x2, x3) actions with a Diophantine question. The Littlewood problem itself dates from about 1930 (Wikipedia, no publication found). Measure-rigidity conjectures: Katok-Spatzier 1996 (doi 10.1017/s0143385700009081), Rudolph 1990 (doi 10.1017/s0143385700005629), Margulis 2000. QUE conjecture: Rudnick-Sarnak 1994 (doi 10.1007/bf02099418). Low agreement on which counts as conceptual.

evidence.claim: Einsiedler, Katok and Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood conjecture, Ann. of Math. 164 (2006) 513-560
Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 165-219

methodological.note: Both papers appeared in 2006 (preprints circulated earlier; Lindenstrauss also has Current Developments in Mathematics 2004, doi 10.4310/cdm.2004.v2004.n1.a4). The exceptional set has Hausdorff dimension zero.

evidence.claim: Paper title naming the transfer: Einsiedler and Kleinbock, Measure rigidity and p-adic Littlewood-type problems, Compos. Math. 143 (2007)
Textbook: Einsiedler and Ward, Ergodic theory with a view towards number theory, GTM 259 (2011)

institutional.note: zbMATH ti:"measure rigidity" 1990-2010: 12 hits, earliest Ratner 1990 (unipotent case, not the diagonal transfer). ti:"Littlewood conjecture" hits before 2005 are mostly the unrelated L1-norm Littlewood conjecture. Earliest indexed title only.

works.citation: Einsiedler, M.; Katok, A.; Lindenstrauss, E. Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood conjecture. Ann. of Math. 164 (2006).
Einsiedler, M.; Ward, T. Ergodic theory with a view towards number theory. GTM 259, Springer (2011).
Katok, A.; Spatzier, R. Invariant measures for higher-rank hyperbolic abelian actions. Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 16 (1996).
Einsiedler, M.; Katok, A.; Lindenstrauss, E. Ann. of Math. 164 (2006).
Lindenstrauss, E. Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity. Ann. of Math. 163 (2006).
Einsiedler, M.; Katok, A.; Lindenstrauss, E. Ann. of Math. 164 (2006).
Furstenberg, H. Disjointness in ergodic theory, minimal sets, and a problem in Diophantine approximation. Math. Systems Theory 1 (1967).
works.whyItMatters: x2 x3 rigidity and Diophantine link.

works.citation: Margulis, G. Problems and conjectures in rigidity theory. In Mathematics: frontiers and perspectives, AMS (2000) 161-174.
works.whyItMatters: States measure-rigidity conjectures for diagonal actions.

notes: Partial result only: Littlewood conjecture remains open. QUE result needs an extra Bourgain-Lindenstrauss entropy input (not checked here). Contents of Margulis 2000 not read; its link to Littlewood is from secondary knowledge and flagged low.

canonicalName: Old Babylonian quadratic and cubic problem-solving

evidence.claim: Most recovered mathematical tablets date 1800-1600 BC and include quadratic and cubic equations
Rectangle-area problems lead to quadratics; excavation volume problems lead to cubics

conceptual.note: No publication date: school tablets dated by archaeological period (Old Babylonian period given as 2000-1600 or 1830-1531 BC on Wikipedia). Range reflects the bulk of datable tablets, not an individual text.

evidence.claim: Tablet BM 85200+ with 36 excavation problems is the earliest known attempt to set up and solve cubics
Neugebauer, Uber die Losung kubischer Gleichungen in Babylonien, Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen 1933 (modern analysis)

methodological.note: Same tablets as conceptual; individual tablet dates (BM 13901, BM 85200+) not verified, so range is period-level and low confidence.

institutional.note: No named discipline in the period. Modern scholarship naming it: Neugebauer 1932 Studien zur Geschichte der antiken Algebra I (zbMATH 0004.00203); Neugebauer, Mathematische Keilschrift-Texte 1935-37 (zbMATH 61.0008.05); Thureau-Dangin, Textes mathematiques babyloniens 1938 (zbMATH 0022.09703); Gandz 1937 Osiris (doi 10.1086/368481); Hoyrup 2002 Lengths, Widths, Surfaces (doi 10.1007/978-1-4757-3685-4). zbMATH ti:"Babylonian algebra" 1900-1960: 0 hits. These are historiographic, not institutional dates of the event.

works.citation: Neugebauer, O. Uber die Losung kubischer Gleichungen in Babylonien. Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen, Math.-Phys. Kl. 1933, 316-321.
Neugebauer, O. Mathematische Keilschrift-Texte I-II. Quellen und Studien A 3 (1935).
Neugebauer, O. Studien zur Geschichte der antiken Algebra I. Quellen und Studien B 2 (1932).
works.whyItMatters: Early framing of Babylonian procedures as algebra.

notes: Ancient scribes anonymous. Interpretation contested: Hoyrup (2002) reads the procedures as naive cut-and-paste geometry rather than algebra in the symbolic sense; Neugebauer framed them as algebra. Thureau-Dangin omitted as a person because no biography page was checked.

evidence.claim: Archimedes lived 287-212 BC; works include On plane equilibriums and On floating bodies
On Floating Bodies thought to be written near the end of his life

conceptual.note: Range is the lifespan bracket; no datable publication. Terminus ante quem 212 BC.

evidence.claim: Equilibrium of planes sets out mechanics principles by geometric methods, finding centres of gravity of plane figures; Floating Bodies founds hydrostatics
Heath, The works of Archimedes (1897), English edition of the treatises

methodological.note: Same treatises perform the application; dated only by lifespan.

institutional.note: No ancient institutional marker found. Searched: MacTutor Archimedes biography, Wikipedia On Floating Bodies, zbMATH (Heath 1897 edition, Dijksterhuis 1938 monograph zbMATH 64.0010.01). Pappus mentions a lost treatise On balances and levers (MacTutor). Later naming of statics as a discipline not researched.

works.citation: Archimedes. The works of Archimedes, ed. in modern notation by T. L. Heath. Cambridge University Press (1897).
works.whyItMatters: Contains On the Equilibrium of Planes and On Floating Bodies; modern edition, not original date.

notes: Some propositions of Equilibrium of Planes I may be later reconstructions (MacTutor cites Berggren 1976/77 on spurious theorems). Whether the lever proof is circular is a long-running dispute (MacTutor references). Ancient dates cannot be pinned below lifespan.

evidence.claim: Dedekind introduced the term Korper and prime ideals in 1871
Dirichlet, Vorlesungen uber Zahlentheorie, 2nd ed. by Dedekind, Braunschweig: Vieweg (1871)

conceptual.note: Dedekind field concept is for subfields of C, not abstract. Abstract definitions: Weber 1893 (Math. Ann. 43, doi 10.1007/bf01446451) for groups and fields; Steinitz 1910 per MacTutor gave the first abstract definition of a field. Ring term: Hilbert Zahlring, Zahlbericht 1897 (zbMATH 28.0157.05).

evidence.claim: Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Korper, J. reine angew. Math. 137 (1910) 167ff.
Steinitz 1910: prime fields, separability, transcendence degree, algebraic closure for every field
Fraenkel, Uber die Teiler der Null und die Zerlegung von Ringen, J. reine angew. Math. 145 (1915)
evidence.source: Crossref record (thesis examined January 1914 per MacTutor)

evidence.claim: Noether, Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen, Math. Ann. 83 (1921)

methodological.note: Steinitz is the first systematic use of the abstract field concept to classify all fields. For rings: Fraenkel axioms 1914/15 (often cited 1914; Crossref volume year 1915), Noether 1921 ideal theory in abstract rings.

evidence.claim: van der Waerden, Moderne Algebra I (1930), II (1931), Grundlehren
Moderne Algebra volume I 1930, volume II 1931, based on Noether and Artin lectures
evidence.source: MacTutor biography of van der Waerden

institutional.note: Textbook naming the abstract approach. Weber Lehrbuch der Algebra (1895) is earlier but MacTutor notes it treated fields and groups as tools, not theories.

works.citation: Dirichlet, P. G. L. Vorlesungen uber Zahlentheorie, 2nd ed., ed. R. Dedekind (with supplements). Vieweg (1871).

Fraenkel date: thesis examined 1914, journal volume 145 dated 1915 by Crossref. MacTutor ring page says axiomatic commutative ring theory came in the 1920s (Noether, Krull).

canonicalName: Arbuthnot sex-ratio argument as an early significance test

evidence.claim: Arbuthnot, An argument for divine providence, taken from the constant regularity observed in the births of both sexes, Phil. Trans. 27 (1710)
Paper submitted 1710 on male excess in London births 1629-1710; called perhaps the first formal significance test
Same paper applies a chance (coin-toss) calculation to 82 years of christening data

methodological.note: The paper itself performs the test; 82-year span from MacTutor date range 1629-1710.

evidence.claim: Fisher, Statistical methods for research workers (1925), textbook of significance testing
Earliest zbMATH title with "tests of significance": Fisher 1929, Proc. R. Soc. A 125
evidence.source: zbMATH search ti:"tests of significance" 1900-1935 (9 hits)

institutional.note: Fisher 1925 chosen as first textbook; its use of the phrase was not checked inside the book. Crossref title search for "test of significance" before 1929 gave only medical/chemical uses. zbMATH/JFM coverage of statistics journals before 1930 is incomplete (Biometrika, JRSS), so earlier titles may exist.

works.citation: Arbuthnot, J. An argument for divine providence, taken from the constant regularity observed in the births of both sexes. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. 27 (1710).
Fisher, R. A. Statistical methods for research workers. Oliver and Boyd (1925).

works.citation: Fisher, R. A. Tests of significance in harmonic analysis. Proc. R. Soc. A 125 (1929) 54-59.
works.whyItMatters: Earliest indexed title using the phrase.

notes: MacTutor says the paper prompted controversy (Shoesmith); responses by s Gravesande and Nicholas Bernoulli are known from secondary literature but were not verified here. Calling it the first significance test is a later historiographic judgement.

Leray worked only on topology as prisoner 1940-45 (Oflag XVIIA); Miller 2000 on origins of sheaf theory cited
